title_en: The majlis record: who is speaking?
q_en: In a record of a majlis, whose words am I reading: the writer’s or the teacher’s? Which little formulas tell me?
q_ar: مَنِ الَّذِي يَتَكَلَّمُ فِي مَا كُتِبَ عَنِ الْمَجْلِسِ؟ وَكَيْفَ أَعْرِفُ كَلَامَ الشَّيْخِ مِنْ كَلَامِ الْكَاتِبِ؟
not_yet: How scholars test whether a record is reliable: that belongs to the study of sources.
Every formula used for every kind of teacher: you will meet them one by one, by reading.
Reading a record with no vowels at all: you begin with one paragraph in this exercise, and it grows.
not_yet_ar: كَيْفَ يَخْتَبِرُ الْعُلَمَاءُ صِحَّةَ السِّجِلِّ: هَذَا مِنْ عِلْمِ الْمَصَادِرِ.
كُلُّ التَّعَابِيرِ لِكُلِّ شَيْخٍ: تَلْقَاهَا وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ.
قِرَاءَةُ سِجِلٍّ بِلَا حَرَكَاتٍ: تَبْدَأُ بِفِقْرَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فِي التَّمْرِينِ، ثُمَّ تَزِيدُ.

slides.head_ar: اُنْظُرْ: خَمْسَةُ أَسْطُرٍ مِنْ دَفْتَرِ الْمَجْلِسِ
sents: The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
وَقَالَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: الصَّبْرُ جَمِيلٌ.
And he said, may Allah be pleased with him: Patience is beautiful.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: اُطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
The Habib said, as to the sense: Seek knowledge.
سَمِعْنَا مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: إِنَّ الْمَجْلِسَ نُورٌ.
We heard from the Habib: The majlis is light.
May Allah benefit us by him.

lines: In each line, which words are the writer’s frame, and which words are the teacher’s saying? Look for the colon.
فِي كُلِّ سَطْرٍ: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ هِيَ إِطَارُ الْكَاتِبِ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ هِيَ كَلَامُ الشَّيْخِ؟ اُنْظُرْ إِلَى النُّقْطَتَيْنِ.
Line 3 says مَا مَعْنَاهُ. Does the writer promise the exact words?
السَّطْرُ ٣ فِيهِ «مَا مَعْنَاهُ». هَلْ يَعِدُ الْكَاتِبُ بِالْأَلْفَاظِ نَفْسِهَا؟
Which line is not a saying at all, but a prayer?
أَيُّ سَطْرٍ لَيْسَ كَلَامًا مَنْقُولًا بَلْ دُعَاءً؟

slides.note: After رَضِيَ the little word عَنْ means “with”: رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ = Allah was pleased with him.
slides.note_ar: بَعْدَ «رَضِيَ» تَأْتِي «عَنْ»: رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ = كَانَ اللَّهُ رَاضِيًا عَنْهُ.

slides.tip: The frame belongs to the writer. Only what follows the colon belongs to the teacher.

Ahmad wrote down the Habib’s speech in his book.
The Habib said: Provision is from Allah.
Allah benefited the student by his knowledge.
The Habib’s speech benefited the people.

items: may Allah be pleased with him
may Allah benefit us by him

slides.why: A learner reads: “he was pleased with Allah”. But اللَّهُ ends in ـُ: it is the one who was pleased. It means: Allah was pleased with him. Say it as the writer’s prayer, not as part of the saying.
slides.why_ar: قَرَأَ الطَّالِبُ: «رَضِيَ هُوَ عَنِ اللَّهِ». وَلَكِنَّ «اللَّهُ» مَرْفُوعٌ، فَهُوَ الَّذِي رَضِيَ. الْمَعْنَى: رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ. وَهَذَا دُعَاءُ الْكَاتِبِ، لَيْسَ مِنْ كَلَامِ الشَّيْخِ.

slides.head_en: A page of a record: the first saying
slides.head_ar: صَفْحَةٌ مِنْ سِجِلِّ مَجْلِسٍ: الْقَوْلُ الْأَوَّلُ
lines: وَقَالَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا قَدْرُ كِفَايَتِهِ فَقَطْ بِلَا زِيَادَةٍ فَذَاكَ رِزْقُهُ الْمُقَدَّرُ لَهُ
And he, God be pleased with him, said, as to the sense: whoever has of this world just enough for his needs, with no extra, that is his appointed provision;
أَوْ زَائِدٌ فَمَا فَوْقَ ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ رِزْقُ غَيْرِهِ اسْتُخْلِفَ فِيهِ، وَهُوَ عِنْدَهُ أَمَانَةٌ
or, if there is more, then what is above that is the provision of someone else, of which he was made steward, and it is a trust with him;
فَلْيُرَاعِ فِيهِ مَا يَلْزَمُهُ وَكَمَا يَنْبَغِي عَلَى مُقْتَضَى الشَّرْعِ، وَيَتَصَدَّقْ مِنْهُ وَيُقَدِّمْ مِنْهُ لِآخِرَتِهِ
so let him observe in it what is due, as is fitting according to the law, and give charity from it and send some ahead for his hereafter.

sections.name: A
sections.en: A page of a record of a majlis: the second saying. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: وَقَالَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ: سَمِعْنَا فِيمَا بَلَغَنَا: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلَائِكَةً مُوَكَّلِينَ بِخَزَائِنِ أَرْزَاقِ الْعِبَادِ
And he, God be pleased with him, said: We have heard, in what has reached us, that God has angels put in charge of the stores of the servants' provisions,
وَإِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا
and that the servant has in every moment a known provision.
فَإِذَا أَطَاعَ الْعَبْدُ رَبَّهُ وَأَحْسَنَ لَهُ الْمُعَامَلَةَ أَمَرَ اللهُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ الْمُوَكَّلِينَ بِخَزَائِنِ أَرْزَاقِ الْعِبَادِ أَنْ يُعَجِّلُوا لَهُ مِنْ رِزْقِهِ فِي الْوَقْتِ الْآتِي
So when the servant obeys his Lord and deals well with Him, God commands the angels in charge of the stores to hasten for him some of his provision of the coming time,
مَعَ رِزْقِهِ فِي الْوَقْتِ الْحَاضِرِ، فَيَتَّسِعُ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فِيهِ
together with his provision of the present time, so his provision widens for him in it.
وَإِذَا عَصَى وَأَسَاءَ الْمُعَامَلَةَ أَمَرَ الْخَزَنَةَ وَقَالَ: ادَّخِرُوا رِزْقَ هَذَا لَهُ فِي الْخَزَائِنِ
And when he disobeys and deals badly, He commands the keepers and says: store this one's provision for him in the stores.
sections.source: Tathbīt al-Fuʾād bi-dhikr majālis al-Quṭb ʿAbdallāh al-Ḥaddād, collected by Aḥmad b. ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Ḥasāwī al-Shajjār
sections.cite: Aḥmad b. ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Ḥasāwī, Tathbīt al-Fuʾād bi-dhikr majālis al-Quṭb ʿAbdallāh al-Ḥaddād, Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih Sufi library, id 184280, 734 pp, digital; no publisher or year; also an epub in TLNOOR 697 and a three-volume OCR PDF in TLNOOR 905–907), page 100 of the copy (digital pagination: the page column equals the record id); printed edition not identified. Lines 4-8 of the page (the second saying; lines 1-3 are on the slides). The copy is unvowelled: vowelled for learners by the course, a letter-for-letter match with the copy. In the line beginning مَعَ رِزْقِهِ the verb فَيَتَّسِعُ is read as the start of a new clause (indicative); the other reading is فَيَتَّسِعَ (subjunctive).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them. Line 4 (the fourth line of the panel) begins a new clause with فَيَتَّسِعُ (indicative); the other possible reading, فَيَتَّسِعَ, gives the same meaning here.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A record of a majlis: sayings of Imam al-Ḥaddād, written down by a student, from Tathbīt al-Fuʾād.

items.en: Which words open the passage and show that someone else is speaking?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَفْتَحُ النَّصَّ وَتَدُلُّ عَلَى مُتَكَلِّمٍ آخَرَ؟

items.en: What do these words tell you about how the teacher knows what he says next?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتُ عَنْ مَصْدَرِ مَا يَقُولُهُ بَعْدَهَا؟
items.model: He says it reached him from others (“we heard in what has reached us”): he reports it, he does not claim it as his own discovery.

items.en: Translate line 1.
items.model: And he said, God be pleased with him: We have heard, in what has reached us, that God has angels put in charge of the stores of the servants’ provisions,

items.en: Translate line 2.

and that the servant has in every moment a known provision.
items.answer: and that the servant has in every moment a known provision.
items.model: and that the servant has in every moment a known provision.

items.en: Translate line 3.
items.model: So when the servant obeys his Lord and deals well with Him, God commands the angels in charge of the stores to hasten for him some of his provision of the coming time,

items.ar: وَإِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا
items.en: True or false: the servant’s provision is not known.
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: رِزْقُ الْعَبْدِ غَيْرُ مَعْلُومٍ.

items.note: The provision is مَعْلُومًا, known (to God, who has set it).

items.en: What does God command the angels when the servant obeys?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا يَأْمُرُ اللَّهُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ إِذَا أَطَاعَ الْعَبْدُ؟
items.model: To hasten for him some of the provision of the coming time, together with that of the present time.

items.en: What happens to the servant’s provision then?
options: أَرْزَاقِ is the plural of رِزْق
and that the servant has in every moment a known provision.
items.model: It widens for him.

items.en: What happens when the servant disobeys and deals badly? What is commanded?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا يَحْدُثُ إِذَا عَصَى الْعَبْدُ وَأَسَاءَ الْمُعَامَلَةَ؟
items.model: God commands the keepers: store this one’s provision for him in the stores.

items.en: Who says ادَّخِرُوا, and to whom? How can you tell it is a quotation inside the quotation?
items.ar_q: مَنْ يَقُولُ «ادَّخِرُوا»؟ وَلِمَنْ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ أَنَّهُ كَلَامٌ دَاخِلَ كَلَامٍ؟
items.model: God says it to the keepers. وَقَالَ and the colon open it, inside the teacher’s own report.

items.en: Find the word that means “provisions” in line 1. What is its singular, and what lesson taught it?
items.ar_q: جِدْ كَلِمَةَ «أَرْزَاقٍ» فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ. مَا مُفْرَدُهَا؟
options: أَرْزَاقِ is the plural of رِزْق
and that the servant has in every moment a known provision.
items.answer: أَرْزَاقِ is the plural of رِزْق
items.model: أَرْزَاقِ is the plural of رِزْق (this lesson).

items.en: ★ Both halves speak of obeying and disobeying. What does each half teach about provision?
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا يُعَلِّمُ كُلُّ نِصْفٍ عَنِ الرِّزْقِ؟
items.model: Obedience brings provision sooner and wider; disobedience delays it. In both, the provision is already decreed: the servant’s conduct changes when it reaches him.

items.en: ★ The writer uses “God be pleased with him” and “we heard in what reached us” in one passage. Why does a careful record keep these formulas?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا يَحْفَظُ السِّجِلُّ الدَّقِيقُ هَذَيْنِ التَّعْبِيرَيْنِ؟
items.model: The first marks whose saying it is, with respect; the second tells the reader how far the teacher himself stands behind the report. A reader sees both the speaker and the source.

sections.name: B
sections.en: A short text: the notebook of Ahmad. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحَبِيبِ.
After the prayer Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s majlis.
فَتَحَ أَحْمَدُ كِتَابَهُ وَكَتَبَ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ.
Ahmad opened his book and wrote down the Habib’s speech.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الرِّزْقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ، فَاشْكُرِ اللَّهَ.
The Habib said: Provision is from Allah, so thank Allah.
ثُمَّ قَالَ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ شَكَرَ اللَّهَ أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ رِزْقًا كَثِيرًا.
Then he said, as to the sense: Whoever thanks Allah, Allah gives him much provision.
وَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ أَحْمَدَ: لِمَاذَا كَتَبْتَ «مَا مَعْنَاهُ»؟
And Umar asked Ahmad: Why did you write “as to the sense”?
قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: لِأَنِّي سَمِعْتُ الْمَعْنَى وَلَمْ أَحْفَظْ كُلَّ الْكَلِمَاتِ.
Ahmad said: Because I heard the meaning and did not memorise every word.
فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: حَسَنٌ، اُكْتُبْ مَا سَمِعْتَ، وَلَا تَكْتُبْ مَا لَمْ تَسْمَعْ.
The Habib said: Good. Write what you heard, and do not write what you did not hear.
وَبَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ لِعُمَرَ: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِالْحَبِيبِ وَبِكَلَامِهِ.
After the lesson Ahmad said to Umar: May Allah benefit us by the Habib and by his speech.
وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ لِأُمِّهِ.
He returned to the house and read the Habib’s speech to his mother.
وَقَالَتْ أُمُّهُ: نَفَعَكَ اللَّهُ يَا بُنَيَّ.
And his mother said: May Allah benefit you, my son.

sections.name: C
sections.en: One paragraph with no vowels: a record of the Habib’s majlis. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: إِنَّ لِلطَّالِبِ أَدَبًا مَعَ مُعَلِّمِهِ.
And the Habib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The student has manners to keep with his teacher.
فَمَنْ جَلَسَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَلْيَسْمَعْ، وَلَا يَتَكَلَّمْ كَثِيرًا.
So whoever sits in the majlis, let him listen, and let him not talk much.
وَقَالَ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ عَمِلَ بِعِلْمِهِ نَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ بِهِ.
And he said, as to the sense: Whoever acts on his knowledge, Allah benefits him by it.
وَسَمِعْنَا مِنْهُ أَنَّ الرِّزْقَ مِنَ اللَّهِ، وَأَنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ رِزْقًا فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ.
And we heard from him that provision is from Allah, and that the servant has a provision in every time.
May Allah benefit us by him and by his speech.

سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.
And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.
رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.
فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.
اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ.
The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk.
Then he sat and strove in his wird.
The boy never missed the rawḥa.
يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.
A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.
بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib.
It is a small book that I read three times.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ.
The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ كَيْ يَعْمَلَ بِعِلْمِهِ.
The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.
The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns.
وَإِذَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ.
And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.
The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary.
ثُمَّ قَالَ: الْحِكْمَةُ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ.
The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel.
وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ النَّصِيحَةُ.
And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ.
The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it.
ثُمَّ دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.
Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ مِنَ الْمَتْنِ: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ.
In the rawḥa the Habib read from the matn: Raising the hands is recommended in four places.
ثُمَّ سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا حُكْمُ رَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ؟ فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ: سُنَّةٌ.
Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands? The boy said: A sunna.
قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً فِي الْبَيْتِ وَسَمِعَهَا الْوَلَدُ.
Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her.
She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
قَالَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا.
The boy’s father said: My son, hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.
And hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping a promise.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ نَصِيحَةً طَوِيلَةً عَنِ التَّقْوَى.
The Habib read a long counsel about taqwā (God-consciousness).
وَمَعْنَاهَا: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى سَبِيلٌ إِلَيْهِ.
And its meaning: There is no good, present or future, but taqwā is a road to it.
قَرَأَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ الرَّاتِبَ بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ وَحَضَرَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَهُمْ.
The people of Tarim read the Rātib after ʿIshāʾ, and the boy attended with them.
وَقَالُوا: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ثَلَاثًا.
And they said: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created (three times).
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ اِجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gathered in the mosque.
وَقَرَأَ الْجَمِيعُ الْمَوْلِدَ وَذَكَرُوا جَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَكَمَالَهُ.
And everyone read the mawlid and they mentioned the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
The boy heard in the majlis a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.
And in every verse there is a first half and a second half.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ سِيرَةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: وُلِدَ فِي مَكَّةَ وَنَشَأَ يَتِيمًا وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ.
The boy read the life of the Prophet ﷺ: He was born in Mecca, grew up an orphan, and his grandfather took him in his care.
So the boy loved the Prophet ﷺ even more.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً مِنْ رَسَائِلِ الْإِمَامِ.
The boy copied out a letter from the letters of the Imam.
وَكَانَ فِي أَوَّلِهَا: وَبَعْدُ، وَفِي آخِرِهَا: وَالسَّلَامُ.
At its beginning was: “And now”, and at its end: “And peace”.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: إِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا.
The Habib said, in meaning: The servant has in every moment a known provision.
وَكَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ.
And the boy wrote that down and said: May Allah benefit us through him.

items.en: Translate the two new lines into English.
items.model: The Habib said, in meaning: The servant has in every moment a known provision. And the boy wrote that down and said: May Allah benefit us through him.

items.en: What does مَا مَعْنَاهُ tell the reader?
items.model: That these are words to this effect: the meaning is given, not word for word.

items.en: What does نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ mean?
items.model: May Allah benefit us through him.

items.en: Write in Arabic: The boy wrote what he heard.
items.model: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ.
